title: Former Delhi Minister Satyendar Jain Arrested in Delhi Jal Board Corruption Case
excerpt: The AAP leader's arrest in the Rs 1,943-crore sewage treatment plant scam marks his second detention by enforcement agencies in four years.
body:
• Former AAP minister Satyendar Jain arrested in connection with alleged corruption in Delhi Jal Board sewage treatment plant contracts worth Rs 1,943 crore
  • The Enforcement Directorate had filed a chargesheet against Jain and 13 others in December 2025 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act
  • Investigation alleges inflated project costs, rigged tenders, and Rs 6.73 crore in illegal commissions paid through banking channels and cash
  • Jain was previously arrested in a separate money laundering case in May 2022 and released on interim bail in 2023

Former Delhi minister and Aam Aadmi Party leader Satyendar Jain has been arrested in connection with the Delhi Jal Board corruption case, according to multiple reports from The Indian Express, NDTV, and The Times of India. The arrest marks his second detention by central enforcement agencies in four years.

Jain, who served as Delhi's water minister and chairman of the Delhi Jal Board under the Arvind Kejriwal-led government, faces allegations of involvement in a Rs 1,943-crore scam related to the upgrade and expansion of 10 sewage treatment plants across Delhi.

The Delhi Jal Board Scandal

The case stems from an FIR registered by Delhi's Anti-Corruption Branch against Hyderabad-based Euroteck Environmental Pvt. Ltd. and others. According to the Enforcement Directorate, four tenders were floated in October 2022 for sewage treatment plant upgrades, but only three joint venture companies participated — allegedly colluding to divide the work among themselves.

The tender conditions were reportedly manipulated to exclude competition, favoring pre-selected players. The project cost, initially estimated at Rs 1,546 crore, was later revised upward to Rs 1,943 crore. The participating companies eventually sub-contracted the entire work to Euroteck, which ED alleges lacked the competence to execute it.

"Rajakumar Kurra and his associates paid illegal commission and a bribe of Rs 6.73 crore through banking channels and in cash, which is nothing but Proceeds of Crime under PMLA."

— Enforcement Directorate statement

ED's investigation also found that the participating companies used the same Taiwan-based project certificates to prove experience, without any verification by authorities. Raids conducted across Delhi, Ahmedabad, Mumbai, and Hyderabad led to the seizure of Rs 41 lakh in cash and incriminating documents.

A Long Trail of Legal Troubles

The Delhi Jal Board case is the third money laundering investigation in which the ED has probed Jain's role. In December 2025, the agency filed a formal chargesheet against Jain and 13 others, including former DJB CEO Udit Prakash Rai, ex-DJB member Ajay Gupta, and former chief engineer Satish Chandra Vashishth.

Jain was first arrested by the ED in May 2022 in a separate PMLA case based on a CBI complaint alleging he acquired disproportionate assets between 2015 and 2017. He was released on interim bail in 2023 on health grounds. In July 2026, he was questioned by the ED at its headquarters in connection with the DJB case.

In a rare bright spot for Jain, a Delhi court in 2025 closed a separate corruption case after the CBI found no evidence of wrongdoing, with the judge ruling that "suspicion cannot replace proof."

AAP's Response

The Aam Aadmi Party has consistently denied wrongdoing, calling the cases politically motivated. In previous statements, former Delhi Chief Minister Atishi alleged that "BJP agencies levelled false allegations" against Jain, noting that "more than 200 cases were filed against AAP leaders in 10 years, but to date, not a single rupee of corruption has been recovered."

AAP has maintained that Jain had already been arrested in May 2022 and was a minister without portfolio when the DJB tenders were awarded in October 2022, questioning the ED's locus standi in the case.

What's Next

The arrest is likely to reignite the political battle between AAP and the BJP-led central government, which controls the Enforcement Directorate. Jain's legal team is expected to challenge the arrest in court. The case will be closely watched as it intersects with the broader question of whether anti-corruption agencies are being used as political tools — a charge both ruling and opposition parties routinely level against each other in Indian politics.
nri_angle: The arrest adds to AAP's mounting legal troubles, a closely watched political saga for diaspora Indians following Delhi politics.
